title: Keggin-Type H<sub>5</sub>PMo<sub>10</sub>V<sub>2</sub>O<sub>40</sub> Intercalated MgAl-LDH: Structural Integrity and Bifunctional Electrocatalytic Activity
authors: Pushparaj Loganathan, Kalathiparambil Rajendra Pai Sunajadevi, Devaraj Muthukumar
abstract: Keggin-type polyoxometalates (H₅PMo₁₀V₂O₄₀) intercalated into MgAl layered double hydroxides (LDH) display exceptional structural integrity and robust bifunctional electrocatalytic performance for overall water splitting in alkaline media. The strong electrostatic interaction between the anionic Keggin POM units and the cationic LDH layers prevents active site aggregation and dissolution. Electrochemical measurements demonstrate low overpotentials for oxygen evolution reaction (OER) and hydrogen evolution reaction (HER), along with long-term durability over 100 hours of continuous operation.
keyFindings: Bifunctional electrocatalytic activity for both OER and HER
Intercalation maintains structural stability during prolonged electrocatalysis
Synergistic electron transfer across the POM-LDH heterojunction

title: Utilizing Highly Reactive Lewis Pairs Generated by Oxygen Vacancies in the Cu<sub>3</sub>Mo<sub>2</sub>O<sub>9</sub> Solid Catalyst for Cycloaddition of CO<sub>2</sub> to 1,2-Propanediol
authors: S. Sujith, B. J. Vaishnavi, K. M. Rajashekhar Vaibhava, Kalathiparambil Rajendra Pai Sunajadevi, Ganapati V. Shanbhag
abstract: Highly reactive frustrated Lewis pairs created by oxygen vacancies in Cu₃Mo₂O₉ catalysts facilitate efficient cycloaddition of CO₂ to 1,2-propanediol under solvent-free conditions. The synergistic interaction between copper Lewis acid sites and oxygen-vacancy-induced basic sites activates both the epoxide ring and CO₂ molecules simultaneously, achieving high turnover frequency (TOF) and excellent selectivity toward cyclic carbonate products with outstanding catalyst recyclability.
keyFindings: Oxygen-vacancy engineered Lewis acid-base active sites
High catalytic conversion of industrial CO₂ into cyclic carbonate
Excellent reusability and catalyst stability over multiple cycles

title: Harnessing MOF Derived Frustrated Lewis Pair-CeO<sub>2</sub> Nano Catalyst for CO<sub>2</sub>-Activated Soft Oxidation of Furfural to Furoic Acid
authors: S. Sujith, H. K. Meghana, M. Harsha, B. J. Vaishnavi, Chaitra N. Mallannavar, Kalathiparambil Rajendra Pai Sunajadevi, Ganapati V. Shanbhag
abstract: MOF-templated synthesis of CeO₂ nanocatalysts with active frustrated Lewis pairs enables CO₂-promoted soft oxidation of biomass-derived furfural into furoic acid. The MOF-derived ceria architecture provides abundant surface oxygen vacancies and coordinatively unsaturated Ce³⁺ sites that serve as frustrated Lewis pairs, enabling mild, selective oxidation under ambient pressure and mild temperatures without requiring harsh chemical oxidants.
keyFindings: MOF derivative featuring tailored Frustrated Lewis Pair active sites
CO₂-activated catalytic pathway for mild biomass oxidation
High yield conversion of furfural to value-added furoic acid

title: ZIF-8/LDH Nanohybrids for Dye Adsorption: LDH Composition-Dependent Structure and Adsorption Performance
authors: Pushparaj Loganathan, Kalathiparambil Rajendra Pai Sunajadevi, Marimuthu Priyadarshini, Cheriyan John, Sankar Sathish, Kanakarasu Dharmaraj
abstract: ZIF-8 MOF integrated with layered double hydroxide (LDH) nanohybrids presents tailored porosity and composition-dependent structural stability for rapid dye decontamination. The heterostructure exhibits enhanced adsorption capacities for anionic and cationic organic dyes from industrial wastewater, driven by electrostatic interactions, hydrogen bonding, and high specific surface area, showing complete regenerability across multiple adsorption-desorption cycles.
keyFindings: Synergistic composite architecture combining ZIF-8 and LDH
Composition-tunable surface area and active adsorption sites
High removal rates for organic dyes in industrial effluent treatment
